title: Biological activity-profile modeling identifies SARS-CoV-2 antiviral leads
summary: NCATS researchers used biological activity-based modeling (BABM) to infer antiviral activity from compounds’ profiles across multiple assays. Of 311 model-predicted SARS-CoV-2 candidates tested in a live-virus cell-culture assay, 99 were confirmed active (32% hit rate); follow-up assays implicated viral-entry inhibition and/or autophagy modulation among confirmed compounds.
ai_technology: Biological activity-based modeling (BABM) models trained on multi-assay compound-activity profiles
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, NIH; Public Health Agency of Canada; Florida State University

evidence.tested: NCATS researchers used biological activity-based modeling (BABM) to infer antiviral activity from compounds’ profiles across multiple assays.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is from cell-culture live-virus and mechanistic assays, not clinical treatment. 99/311 were active in the primary assay; further potency/secondary confirmations were available for subsets. Most confirmed compounds were reported to inhibit entry and/or modulate autophagy; these data do not establish safe or effective human therapy.
evidence.ai_role: BABM used prior activity signatures across assay panels to predict compounds with potential SARS-CoV-2 activity, including compounds outside conventional similar-structure hit finding. Researchers tested 311 model-predicted compounds in live-virus assays and conducted secondary/mechanistic assays on confirmed actives.
